title: Consistency Pact
concept: A private weekly check: what you say you value, what you meant to do, what you actually did, and one specific change — without needing your partner to watch.
whenToUse: A weekly personal check-in on your own follow-through; after you’ve made an emotional promise; or alongside a shared Proof item while rebuilding trust.
steps: What you say — what do you say you value? Write it down.
What you meant to do — what did you plan to do this week?
What actually happened — where was the gap?
One change — one thing you’ll do differently next week, that you could point to.
Keep it private unless you choose to share it — privacy makes you more honest, not less.
This doesn’t replace being accountable to your partner on a real breach.

phrases.text: Next week I will ___ (something you could point to).

working: You say you’ll repair within 24 hours. You miss it once, so the change becomes: text a same-day apology. The next week, you do it. The gap gets smaller, and your partner can feel it.
notWorking: Doing this privately as a substitute for owning a real breach with your partner. It’s a good habit, but it doesn’t replace being accountable to them.
activity: Write your own private pact. Check in on it once a week for three weeks.
